themes.name: AI's role in enhancing critical thinking skills
themes.definition: The impact of AI tools on developing higher-order cognitive abilities including analysis, evaluation, reasoning, and argumentation across various educational contexts.
evidence: [Busuttil2025] findings reveal that generative AI fosters critical thinking, reflective practices, and the refinement of teaching strategies
[Zhang2025f] integrating AI chatbots into pedagogy can enhance critical thinking skills in argumentative writing
[Al-Shamrani2025] applications of artificial intelligence (ChatGPT) positively impacted the development of critical thinking skills among international students

themes.name: Reconfiguring educational roles with AI
themes.definition: The transformation of traditional educational dynamics as AI assumes multiple functions in learning environments, changing relationships between students, teachers, and knowledge
evidence: [Jho2025] AI performs four key roles: a proactive facilitator, cognitive scaffolder, catalyst, and critical friend
[Naeem2025] ChatGPT served as a peer reviewer to help learners reflect on AI-generated outputs
[Tang2025] generative AI functions as a dialogic partner rather than an authoritative knowledge provider

themes.name: Dual impacts of AI in education
themes.definition: Recognition of both benefits and challenges associated with AI integration, acknowledging the complex interplay between technological advantages and educational requirements
evidence: [Busuttil2025] limitations in linguistic accuracy... require significant human intervention
[Sands2025] initial challenges such as a learning curve while students ultimately gained confidence
[Kim2024b] students developed an overreliance on AI while showing improved critical thinking

themes.name: Critical evaluation of AI-generated content
themes.definition: The active process by which students analyze, verify, and refine AI-generated outputs as a pedagogical approach to develop higher-order thinking skills
evidence: [Sands2025] students had to validate AI outputs and understand estimation principles
[Hong2025a] promoting critical examination of different perspectives with AI tools
[Busuttil2025] need for critical evaluation and customization of AI-generated outputs

themes.name: Structured AI integration frameworks
themes.definition: Systematic pedagogical approaches that deliberately incorporate AI tools with defined methods, rules, or stages to optimize learning outcomes
evidence: [Hong2025b] structured cognitive offload instruction with deliberate scaffolding
[Kim2024b] B.E.A.T.S. program with 5 instructional sessions using AI for music education
[Triana2025] Common Knowledge Constructional Model integrated with AI-Text Generator

data.meta_observations: Three patterns emerged: 1) Critical thinking is most often discussed as multifaceted outcome including analysis, evaluation, and reasoning. 2) Multiple studies emphasize specific roles AI assumes (facilitator, catalyst, etc.). 3) Many studies adopt quasi-experimental designs to measure educational outcomes. A notable gap exists in theoretical frameworks guiding implementation, with most studies being descriptive rather than conceptually driven.
data.grounding_notes: All evidence provided is verbatim as stated in the abstracts. Some themes show high frequency but with varying levels of explicit focus in individual abstracts. 'Critical evaluation of AI-generated content' was mentioned explicitly in 5 abstracts but likely applies more broadly across studies. 'Structured AI integration frameworks' showed clearest evidence in only 3 abstracts despite likely being implied in more.
